summary: Sandboxed code execution (modality 'code'), bounded background jobs, visual computer use (modality 'visual') and a replaceable visual-grounding interface with GoClick-Base, MAI-UI-2B, Vocaela-2-500M and a non-neural baseline, plus a benchmark of all four. Both executors implement contracts.ModalityExecutor and use only ExecContext; neither is wired into harness/env.py by EC (that is the integrator's step) and the authorization layer in the tests is a recording stand-in for PolicyEngine.check_primitive, not workstream EA's service. E-fix: composed into the environment by harness.factories.

IH-03.limitations: Process isolation on the shared host kernel (dedicated uid + rlimits + Landlock ABI 1 + seccomp + no_new_privs), not a VM. Memory is limited per process by RLIMIT_AS; the total of a job and its task count are watched by the per-job monitor every 100 ms (no cgroup available). Disk use is bounded per file and checked against a workspace limit before each operation, not by a quota. Jobs under the same sandbox uid can signal each other. Scoped network: the kernel denies every socket; outbound TCP goes through the egress broker with one ExecContext.check per connection (host, port) made before name resolution; requests reusing a connection and anything inside TLS are not inspected; only Python processes get the transparent shim (curl, git, node have no network). Importable packages inside the sandbox: standard library, numpy, PIL, yaml. multiprocessing locks do not work (/dev/shm is not granted). Not exercised against workstream EA's real policy service or over ExecRPC.

CU-09.limitations: Tested on EC's own Playwright-backed ScreenProvider and a software frame buffer, not on workstream EB's BrowserScreen (same method names; EB's scroll(x=, y=) is used when present). Staleness for pointer actions compares a 73x73 pixel patch around the target (a change elsewhere does not block); keyboard and wheel actions compare the whole frame with a 2 % tolerance. Verification from pixels supports element_state {color_at | changed} and url_matches when the screen has url(); other kinds return verified=None. No OCR. E-fix: the composed visual executor (factories.visual) now runs on EB's BrowserScreen inside ComputerEnvironment: visual.screenshot and visual.click on a browser page, the click's request passing the browser's network guard (test_the_composed_visual_executor_acts_on_the_browsers_screen).

CU-07.limitations: The repository's custom Florence-2 code is not executed: the checkpoint is loaded into transformers' native Florence-2 by renaming tensors (shape-checked), with weight tying switched off. There is no bit-level comparison with the original code (it needs transformers 4.45, timm, einops, none of which is here); equivalence evidence is behavioural (74 of 80 benchmark targets, identical CPU/GPU outputs). The custom code was reviewed by pattern scan and targeted reading, not line by line (about 120 kB unread; it never runs). Its confidence is ~1.0 even on wrong answers.

CU-08.limitations: MAI-UI-2B needs 4.3 GB of GPU memory: the visual executor takes the shared GPU lock for each call and unloads the model before releasing it (about 6 s load + 1.7 s inference per use on this host). Inputs are built by hand because transformers' packaged processor needs torchvision, which is not installed. Used for grounding only; its other output is ignored. Vocaela-2-500M is CC BY-NC-SA 4.0: evaluation only, refuses to load without accept_noncommercial=True and is never in the default order. The escalation from the lightweight to the advanced model inside VisualExecutor is tested with scripted grounders; with the real models it is measured by the benchmark's recovery phase, not by a pytest.

CU-34.limitations: One run, 80 targets on 60 pages generated by EC (canvas buttons, icon-only controls, dense forms, 12-16 px targets, look-alike rows, three-step workflows), one renderer and one visual style, no confidence intervals. Not run on workstream EB's staging sites. Latencies were taken on a machine shared with other jobs (load average 8-10). Recovery is measured as one retry with a fixed fallback grounder on the reproduced failure state. bench.py itself has no pytest; its building blocks do.

not_done: No test uses workstream EA's PolicyService or SecretBroker; the authorization check in every EC test is a recording callable with the check_primitive signature. The primitive names EC sends are listed in docs/change_requests/EC.md for EA.
No test drives VisualExecutor through workstream EB's BrowserScreen; EC's tests use their own Playwright page wrapper as instructed.
No desktop (non-browser) ScreenProvider: this host has no display server.

Kernel-level per-destination network filtering, cgroup memory limits and disk quotas are unavailable in this unprivileged container; the scoped-network broker and the monitor's watchdogs are the substitutes and capabilities() says so. A VM is recommended for live operation.

Scoped network works for Python processes only (socket shim over the broker descriptor); curl, git, pip-less tools and node have no network inside the sandbox. asyncio networking through the shim is untested.
GoClick-Base: no bit-level equivalence check against the publisher's code, and that code was not read line by line (it is never executed).

The lightweight-to-advanced escalation with the real models inside one visual.click_target call is not covered by a pytest (it needs both models and the shared GPU lock); the benchmark's recovery phase measures the same thing with a reproduced failure.
The grounding benchmark was run once, on EC's generated pages only (not on EB's staging sites), without repeated seeds or confidence intervals.
Grounder confidence values are not calibrated; VisualConfig.min_confidence defaults to 0 (no gating).

docs/evidence/EC/grounding_bench.json records the repository HEAD at run time (6d568fe), which predates the final EC commit; the grounding code did not change afterwards except for an internal cleanup hook (close/_release).

E-fix registered SandboxExecutor and VisualExecutor in the composed environment (harness/factories.py) and ran the visual executor on the browser's screen; the sandbox was not exercised through ExecRPC in the separated deployment (it is unavailable there while the executor runs as cambrowser).

E-fix made tests/harness/compute/test_ec_jobs.py::test_status_is_observable_while_running_and_cancel_stops_the_job wait (bounded, 15 s) for the job's child process before counting it: under load average ~25 the child appeared after the job's first output and the test failed once; jobs.py is unchanged.
scientific_failures: The assumption that the larger model is at least as good everywhere did not hold: MAI-UI-2B reached 0.50 on dense forms (it clicked the label instead of the input field in 5 of 10 tasks) where GoClick-Base reached 0.90; overall 0.938 vs 0.925 on 80 targets is not a meaningful difference at this sample size.
GoClick-Base's token-probability confidence is about 1.0 for wrong answers as well, so it cannot be used to decide when to escalate; escalation has to rely on the re-observed effect.
The best model on this benchmark (Vocaela-2-500M, 0.988) cannot be the default because of its non-commercial licence.
